name: Zunami UZD permissionless monotonic rebase price latch
summary: UZD is an elastic rebasing token whose multiplier is PricableAsset._assetPriceCached. The deployed cacheAssetPrice() is public, unguarded, and monotonic: it reads assetPrice(), which is priceOracle.lpPrice() on the immutable Zunami core 0x2ffcc661011bec72e1a9524e12060983e74d14ce, and assigns it whenever it exceeds the stored value, so a single instantaneous reading permanently multiplies every UZD balance. Zunami.lpPrice() is totalHoldings over LP supply summed across strategies at spot, and the MIMCurveStakeDao strategy 0x9848edb097bee96459dff7609fb582b80a8f8efd values whatever SDT sits in it at the SushiSwap SDT/WETH pair price. In the anchor transaction the attacker bought 55,981.929088875410 SDT, transferred it to that strategy, whose totalHoldings() went from 0 to 12,645,055.766381 accounting units, pushed the SushiSwap pair further with a 10,000 WETH swap, and called UZD.cacheAssetPrice() directly. assetPriceCached rose from 912,563,583,136,402,763 to 3,165,200,435,397,696,033, a factor of 3.4685, rebasing the attacker's 4,873,316.59 purchased UZD into 16,902,957.87 sellable UZD; the SushiSwap swap was then unwound in the same transaction while the latch stayed at 3.1652 forever after, confirmed unchanged at block 17960000. The violated invariant is that the rebase multiplier must reflect durable vault backing. The boundary test finds no parameter value that restores it: priceOracle is an immutable constructor argument, and the only related setting, _assetPriceCacheDuration, gates _cacheAssetPriceByBlock() while cacheAssetPrice() stays publicly callable at any block.
notes: UZD is a non-proxy contract created by top-level CREATE; its 14,165-byte runtime is byte-identical at the creation block and immediately before the exploit, and its price oracle is an immutable constructor argument.

The components are the attacker cluster's exact end-of-transaction proceeds, netted from every ERC-20 Transfer log of the anchor receipt for the helper contract 0xa21a2b59d80dc42d332f778cbb9ea127100e5d75 and the sender 0x5f4c21c9bb73c8b4a296cc256c0cde324db146df. Both flash facilities net to zero in that computation: the Balancer loan of 7,000,000 USDC and 10,011 WETH is repaid in full, and the Uniswap V3 USDC/USDT flash of 7,000,000 USDT is repaid with 7,000,710 USDT. The 11 WETH the attacker spent buying the donated SDT is likewise inside the net. The victims are the two Curve UZD pools 0x68934f60758243eafaf4d2cfed27bf8010bede3a and 0xfc636d819d1a98433402ec9dec633d864014f28c, which net out 1,534,228.182865474 3CRV and 641,017.5283662892 crvFRAX against the inflated UZD, plus every remaining UZD holder left with a token whose supply had been multiplied by 3.4685 without backing. The attacker's separate transaction 0x2aec4fdb2a09ad4269a410f2c770737626fb62c54e0fa8ac25e8582d4b690cca 41 blocks earlier ran the identical defect against the code-distinct zETH deployment 0xe47f1cd2a37c6fe69e3501ae45eca263c5a87b2b, which does not appear in this trace; that leg netted the attacker minus 62.840019684438608795 WETH and belongs to its own record, so no part of it is counted here. Nothing was recovered from this transaction.

The record covers only the UZD leg of the campaign. The code-distinct zETH deployment was attacked in a separate transaction that does not execute UZD, so it needs its own incident record and is excluded from this loss.

Zunami's own MIMCurveStakeDao strategy supplied the manipulable spot valuation, so it is a second defect-bearing role in the causal path. It is described in the classification rather than carried as a separate target because the invariant that fails, and the state that made the inflation permanent, both live in the UZD runtime.
